context: FS-009 (the page that asks, AgreementView) is delivered on main and is on this branch. This feature adds Document.enforced, a middleware that redirects a signed-in user with an enforced document outstanding, three settings, one permission, two system checks, and changes when AgreementView lets a person go. The spec amends FS-009's FR-008, FR-012 and FR-018 by design (FR-028 to FR-033): that amendment is approved and is not a finding. Stories are built in dependency order US-2, US-1, US-3, then US-4 to US-6 together (decisions.md D17). T001 is prose only and sits in the ledger under US-2. Standing rules for this repo: no leading-underscore names, line length 88, no compatibility aliases, no test of text content or of layout, no dataclass/registry/settings-generating machinery where a plain Django idiom does, and a mechanism an experienced Django developer would recognise beats a clever one.
orchestrator_question: Verify against the RESOLVED packages and this repo, both sides of each rule. (1) research.md says the session is already loaded when the middleware runs and that reading one key costs no query, and that writing it costs one save on that request only: read django/contrib/sessions and django/contrib/auth/middleware.py and say whether that holds for the db and signed-cookie backends, and whether login()/logout() flushing really stops a stored finding passing from one account to another, including login() for the SAME user and a session that began anonymous. (2) Order of the seven steps in plan.md 'The check': name any input for which a user who should be stopped is served, or a user who should be served is redirected in a loop. Cover: the page that asks routed outside the namespace (demo/urls.py), the package mounted at the site root, a path that resolves to nothing, STATIC_URL or MEDIA_URL set to '/' or to another host or left empty, an entry of the exempt-URLs setting of '/' or '', and request.path versus request.path_info under a script prefix. (3) FR-021 and US-5 scenario 5 are reconciled by decisions.md D15: does any scenario in spec.md contradict that reading? (4) The HX-Redirect answer: check against htmx's documented behaviour whether a 200 with an empty body and HX-Redirect navigates the whole window, and what a 3xx does. (5) AgreementView.get() per plan.md 'The page that asks': walk every scenario of US-3 (12) and FS-009's US-4 against it and name any that fails. (6) Migration: is AddField(default=True) plus AlterModelOptions enough for FR-024 with 0001 already released, and does tests/test_migrations.py's existing design allow the planned backward-then-forward migration test? (7) Coverage, with counts: FR against tasks N of 33, SC against tasks N of 10, scenarios against tasks N of 49. (8) Is any planned test a change detector, or a test of wording or appearance, or one that would pass before its implementing task?
